sanskrit: abhīkṣṇaṃ krūravādinyaḥ paruṣā ruditapriyāḥ bhartṝṇāṃ vacane caiva na sthāsyanti tadā striyaḥ
english: Women will constantly speak harshly, be cruel and fond of weeping, and will no longer abide by their husbands' words.

sanskrit: putrāś ca mātāpitarau haniṣyanti yugakṣaye sūdayiṣyanti ca patīn striyaḥ putrān apāśritāḥ
english: Sons will slay their mothers and fathers at the end of the age; women, relying on their sons, will do away with their husbands.

sanskrit: aparvaṇi mahārāja sūryaṃ rāhur upaiṣyati yugānte hutabhuk cāpi sarvataḥ prajvaliṣyati
english: O great king, at the end of the age Rāhu will seize the sun at an inauspicious time, and fire will blaze up on all sides.

sanskrit: pānīyaṃ bhojanaṃ caiva yācamānās tadādhvagāḥ na lapsyante nivāsaṃ ca nirastāḥ pathi śerate
english: Wayfarers who beg for water and food will find none; turned away, they will sleep on the road.

sanskrit: nirghātavāyasā nāgāḥ śakunāś ca samṛgadvijāḥ rūkṣā vāco vimokṣyanti yugānte paryupasthite
english: As the end of the age draws near, elephants, crows, birds together with deer and twice-born will utter harsh, discordant cries.

sanskrit: mitrasaṃbandhinaś cāpi saṃtyakṣyanti narās tadā janaṃ parijanaṃ cāpi yugānte paryupasthite
english: As the end of the age approaches, men will abandon friends, relatives, and their own dependents.

sanskrit: atha deśān diśaś cāpi pattanāni purāṇi ca kramaśaḥ saṃśrayiṣyanti yugānte paryupasthite
english: As the end of the age draws near, people will gradually take refuge in various regions, directions, towns and old cities.

sanskrit: hā tāta hā sutety evaṃ tadā vācaḥ sudāruṇāḥ vikrośamānaś cānyonyaṃ jano gāṃ paryaṭiṣyati
english: Crying out in terrible voices, 'O father! O son!', people will wander the earth lamenting to one another.

sanskrit: tatas tumulasaṃghāte vartamāne yugakṣaye dvijātipūrvako lokaḥ krameṇa prabhaviṣyati
english: Then, while that tumultuous confusion continues at the end of the age, the world, with the twice-born at its head, will gradually flourish again.

sanskrit: tataḥ kālāntare 'nyasmin punar lokavivṛddhaye bhaviṣyati punar daivam anukūlaṃ yadṛcchayā
english: Then, at another turn of time, for the world's increase, fate will again become favourable of its own accord.

sanskrit: yadā candraś ca sūryaś ca tathā tiṣyabṛhaspatī ekarāśau sameṣyanti prapatsyati tadā kṛtam
english: When the moon, the sun, and likewise Tiṣya and Bṛhaspati meet in one zodiacal sign, the Kṛta age will come again.

sanskrit: kālavarṣī ca parjanyo nakṣatrāṇi śubhāni ca pradakṣiṇā grahāś cāpi bhaviṣyanty anulomagāḥ kṣemaṃ subhikṣam ārogyaṃ bhaviṣyati nirāmayam
english: The rain-cloud will rain in season, the constellations will be auspicious, and the planets will move in their proper, clockwise courses; there will be peace, abundance, good health, and freedom from disease.

sanskrit: kalkir viṣṇuyaśā nāma dvijaḥ kālapracoditaḥ utpatsyate mahāvīryo mahābuddhiparākramaḥ
english: A twice-born man named Kalki Viṣṇuyaśas, urged on by time, will be born — one of great valour and of great intellectual power and heroism.

sanskrit: saṃbhūtaḥ saṃbhalagrāme brāhmaṇāvasathe śubhe manasā tasya sarvāṇi vāhanāny āyudhāni ca upasthāsyanti yodhāś ca śastrāṇi kavacāni ca
english: Born in an auspicious Brahmin settlement in the village of Śambhala, all conveyances, weapons, warriors, arms, and armour will present themselves to him by a mere act of will.

sanskrit: sa dharmavijayī rājā cakravartī bhaviṣyati sa cemaṃ saṃkulaṃ lokaṃ prasādam upaneṣyati
english: He will be a king who conquers by righteousness, a world-ruler, and he will bring this troubled world to serenity.

sanskrit: utthito brāhmaṇo dīptaḥ kṣayāntakṛd udāradhīḥ sa saṃkṣepo hi sarvasya yugasya parivartakaḥ
english: This blazing Brahmin who has arisen, the great-minded one who will put an end to destruction — he is indeed the summary and the turner of the entire age.

sanskrit: sa sarvatra gatān kṣudrān brāhmaṇaiḥ parivāritaḥ utsādayiṣyati tadā sarvān mlecchagaṇān dvijaḥ
english: Surrounded by Brahmins, that twice-born will then eradicate all the hosts of barbarians who have spread everywhere.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tataś corakṣayaṃ kṛtvā dvijebhyaḥ pṛthivīm imām vājimedhe mahāyajñe vidhivat kalpayiṣyati
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: After exterminating the thieves he will duly assign this earth to the twice-born in the great horse-sacrifice rite.

sanskrit: sthāpayitvā sa maryādāḥ svayambhuvihitāḥ śubhāḥ vanaṃ puṇyayaśaḥkarmā jarāvān saṃśrayiṣyati
english: Having re-established the auspicious boundaries ordained by the Self-born, he of pure and glorious deeds will, when grown old, resort to the forest.

sanskrit: tacchīlam anuvartsyante manuṣyā lokavāsinaḥ vipraiś corakśaye caiva kṛte kṣemaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: The people dwelling in the world will follow his virtuous conduct, and once the thieves are destroyed by the Brahmins, there will be peace.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇājināni śaktīś ca triśūlāny āyudhāni ca sthāpayan vipraśārdūlo deśeṣu vijiteṣu ca
english: Installing black antelope skins, lances, tridents, and various weapons in the conquered lands,

sanskrit: saṃstūyamāno viprendrair mānayāno dvijottamān kalkiś cariṣyati mahīṃ sadā dasyuvadhe rataḥ
english: honoured by the lords of Brahmins, respecting the best of twice-born, Kalki will roam the earth, ever intent on slaying brigands.

sanskrit: hā tāta hā sutety evaṃ tās tā vācaḥ sudāruṇāḥ vikrośamānān subhṛśaṃ dasyūn neṣyati saṃkṣayam
english: He will bring to complete destruction those brigands who cry out with such terrible voices: 'O father! O son!'

sanskrit: tato 'dharmavināśo vai dharmavṛddhiś ca bhārata bhaviṣyati kṛte prāpte kriyāvāṃś ca janas tathā
english: Then, O Bhārata, when the Kṛta age arrives, there will be the destruction of unrighteousness and the growth of righteousness, and people will be active in their duties.

sanskrit: ārāmāś caiva caityāś ca taṭākāny avaṭās tathā yajñakriyāś ca vividhā bhaviṣyanti kṛte yuge
english: In the Kṛta age there will be pleasure gardens and sacred trees, lakes and wells, and various sacrificial rites.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāḥ sādhavaś caiva munayaś ca tapasvinaḥ āśramāḥ sahapāṣaṇḍāḥ sthitāḥ satye janāḥ prajāḥ
english: Brahmins, good men, sages and ascetics, hermitages together with their communities — all people and subjects will be established in truth.

sanskrit: jāsyanti sarvabījāni upyamānāni caiva ha sarveṣv ṛtuṣu rājendra sarvaṃ sasyaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: All seeds that are sown will germinate and grow, O king of kings; in every season, all crops will flourish.

sanskrit: narā dāneṣu niratā vrateṣu niyameṣu ca japayajñaparā viprā dharmakāmā mudā yutāḥ pālayiṣyanti rājāno dharmeṇemāṃ vasuṃdharām
english: Men will be devoted to charity, vows, and religious observances; Brahmins will be intent on prayer and sacrifice, eager for righteousness, and full of joy; kings will protect this bountiful earth with justice.

sanskrit: vyavahāraratā vaiśyā bhaviṣyanti kṛte yuge ṣaṭkarmaniratā viprāḥ kṣatriyā rakṣaṇe ratāḥ
english: In the Kṛta age, Vaiśyas will be devoted to trade; Brahmins will be intent on the six duties; Kṣatriyas will be devoted to protection.

sanskrit: śuśrūṣāyāṃ ratāḥ śūdrās tathā varṇatrayasya ca eṣa dharmaḥ kṛtayuge tretāyāṃ dvāpare tathā paścime yugakāle ca yaḥ sa te saṃprakīrtitaḥ
english: Śūdras will be devoted to service and to the three upper varṇas. This is the dharma in the Kṛta age, in the Tretā, in the Dvāpara, and in the last age — all of this has been declared to you.

sanskrit: sarvalokasya viditā yugasaṃkhyā ca pāṇḍava etat te sarvam ākhyātam atītānāgataṃ mayā vāyuproktam anusmṛtya purāṇam ṛṣisaṃstutam
english: O Pāṇḍava, the reckoning of the ages is known to all the world. I have told you all — past and future — recalling the ancient lore spoken by Vāyu and praised by the seers.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃsāramārgā me bahuśaś cirajīvinā dṛṣṭāś caivānubhūtāś ca tāṃs te kathitavān aham
english: Thus the paths of saṃsāra have been seen and experienced by me many times in my long life, and I have told them all to you.

sanskrit: idaṃ caivāparaṃ bhūyaḥ saha bhrātṛbhir acyuta dharmasaṃśayamokṣārthaṃ nibodha vacanaṃ mama
english: Now hear this further word of mine as well, O steadfast one, together with your brothers, for the purpose of removing doubts about dharma.

sanskrit: dharme tvayātmā saṃyojyo nityaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ vara dharmātmā hi sukhaṃ rājā pretya ceha ca nandati
english: You should always unite your soul with dharma, O best of those who uphold dharma, for a king whose soul is righteous rejoices in happiness both here and in the hereafter.

sanskrit: nibodha ca śubhāṃ vāṇīṃ yāṃ pravakṣyāmi te 'nagha na brāhmaṇe paribhavaḥ kartavyas te kadā cana brāhmaṇo ruṣito hanyād api lokān pratijñayā
english: And hear the auspicious word I will speak to you, O sinless one: you must never dishonour a Brahmin, for an enraged Brahmin can burn up whole worlds by his resolve.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca mārkaṇḍeyavacaḥ śrutvā kurūṇāṃ pravaro nṛpaḥ uvāca vacanaṃ dhīmān paramaṃ paramadyutiḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard the words of Mārkaṇḍeya, the foremost king of the Kurus, that wise and supremely splendid one, spoke a supreme word.

sanskrit: kasmin dharme mayā stheyaṃ prajāḥ saṃrakṣatā mune kathaṃ ca vartamāno vai na cyaveyaṃ svadharmataḥ
english: In what dharma should I remain while protecting my subjects, O sage? And how should I conduct myself so as not to fall away from my own dharma?

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca dayāvān sarvabhūteṣu hito rakto 'nasūyakaḥ apatyānām iva sveṣāṃ prajānāṃ rakṣaṇe rataḥ cara dharmaṃ tyajādharmaṃ pitṝn devāṃś ca pūjaya
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Be compassionate to all beings, friendly, affectionate, and free from envy; be devoted to protecting your subjects as if they were your own children. Walk in dharma, abandon adharma, and honour the ancestors and the gods.

sanskrit: pramādād yat kṛtaṃ te 'bhūt saṃyag dānena taj jaya alaṃ te mānam āśritya satataṃ paravān bhava
english: Whatever was done through negligence — conquer that by proper giving. Enough with pride; be always dependent on others (i.e., humble).

sanskrit: vijitya pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ modamānaḥ sukhī bhava eṣa bhūto bhaviṣyaś ca dharmas te samudīritaḥ
english: Having conquered the whole earth, rejoice and be happy. This dharma for you — past and future — has been proclaimed.

sanskrit: na te 'sty aviditaṃ kiṃ cid atītānāgataṃ bhuvi tasmād imaṃ parikleśaṃ tvaṃ tāta hṛdi mā kṛthāḥ
english: There is nothing past or future on earth that you do not know. Therefore, dear one, do not hold this anguish in your heart.

sanskrit: eṣa kālo mahābāho api sarvadivaukasām muhyanti hi prajās tāta kālenābhipracoditāḥ
english: This is Time, O mighty-armed one — even for all the gods. Creatures become bewildered, dear one, when driven on by Time.

sanskrit: mā ca te 'tra vicāro bhūd yan mayoktaṃ tavānagha atiśaṅkya vaco hy etad dharmalopo bhavet tava
english: And let there be no doubt in you about what I have told you, O sinless one; for by doubting these words, there would be a falling away from dharma for you.

sanskrit: jāto 'si prathite vaṃśe kurūṇāṃ bharatarṣabha karmaṇā manasā vācā sarvam etat samācara
english: You were born in the illustrious lineage of the Kurus, O bull of the Bhāratas; fulfil all this in deed, thought, and word.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yat tvayoktaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha vākyaṃ śrutimanoharam tathā kariṣye yatnena bhavataḥ śāsanaṃ vibho
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What you, O best of twice-born, have spoken — words lovely to the ear as scripture — that I will do; I will strive to carry out your command, O lord.

sanskrit: na me lobho 'sti viprendra na bhayaṃ na ca matsaraḥ kariṣyāmi hi tat sarvam uktaṃ yat te mayi prabho
english: I have no greed, O lord of Brahmins, nor fear, nor envy; I will indeed do everything you have said to me, O master.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tasya pāṇḍavasya mahātmanaḥ prahṛṣṭāḥ pāṇḍavā rājan sahitāḥ śārṅgadhanvanā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard the words of that great-souled Pāṇḍava, O king, the Pāṇḍavas were filled with joy, together with Śārṅga-bowed Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: tathā kathāṃ śubhāṃ śrutvā mārkaṇḍeyasya dhīmataḥ vismitāḥ samapadyanta purāṇasya nivedanāt
english: And having heard the auspicious tale told by the wise Mārkaṇḍeya, they were filled with wonder at the narration of that ancient lore.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca bhūya eva brāhmaṇamahābhāgyaṃ vaktum arhasīty abravīt pāṇḍaveyo mārkaṇḍeyam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The son of Pāṇḍu said to Mārkaṇḍeya: 'Please speak again on the great good fortune of Brahmins.'

sanskrit: athācaṣṭa mārkaṇḍeyaḥ
english: Then Mārkaṇḍeya narrated:

sanskrit: ayodhyāyām ikṣvākukulotpannaḥ pārthivaḥ parikṣin nāma mṛgayām agamat
english: A king named Parīkṣit, born of the Ikṣvāku line in Ayodhyā, went out on a hunt.

sanskrit: tam ekāśvena mṛgam anusarantaṃ mṛgo dūram apāharat
english: While he was pursuing a deer with a single horse, the deer led him far away.

sanskrit: athādhvani jātaśramaḥ kṣuttṛṣṇābhibhūtaś ca kasmiṃś cid uddeśe nīlaṃ vanaṣaṇḍam apaśyat tac ca viveśa
english: Then, weary from the road, overcome by hunger and thirst, he saw a dark grove in some spot and entered it.

sanskrit: tatas tasya vanaṣaṇḍasya madhye 'tīva ramaṇīyaṃ saro dṛṣṭvā sāśva eva vyagāhata
english: Then in the middle of that grove, seeing an exceedingly beautiful lake, he plunged in together with his horse.

sanskrit: athāśvastaḥ sa bisamṛṇālam aśvasyāgre nikṣipya puṣkariṇītīre samāviśat
english: Refreshed, he placed lotus stalks before his horse and sat down on the bank of the lotus-pond.

sanskrit: tataḥ śayāno madhuraṃ gītaśabdam aśṛṇot
english: Then, as he lay there, he heard the sweet sound of singing.

sanskrit: sa śrutvācintayat neha manuṣyagatiṃ paśyāmi kasya khalv ayaṃ gītaśabda iti
english: Hearing it, he thought: 'I see no human presence here — whose singing can this be?'

sanskrit: athāpaśyat kanyāṃ paramarūpadarśanīyāṃ puṣpāṇy avacinvatīṃ gāyantīṃ ca
english: Then he saw a maiden of supremely beautiful appearance, gathering flowers and singing.

sanskrit: atha sā rājñaḥ samīpe paryakrāmat
english: Then she walked around close to the king.

sanskrit: tām abravīd rājā kasyāsi subhage tvam iti
english: The king said to her: 'O lovely one, whose are you?'

sanskrit: sā pratyuvāca kanyāsmīti
english: She replied: 'I am a maiden.'

sanskrit: tāṃ rājovāca arthī tvayāham iti
english: The king said to her: 'I desire you.'

sanskrit: athovāca kanyā samayenāhaṃ śakyā tvayā labdhum nānyatheti
english: Then the maiden said: 'You can win me only on one condition — not otherwise.'

sanskrit: tāṃ rājā samayam apṛcchat
english: The king asked her what the condition was.

sanskrit: tataḥ kanyedam uvāca udakaṃ me na darśayitavyam iti
english: Then the maiden said: 'Water must never be shown to me.'

sanskrit: sa rājā bāḍham ity uktvā tāṃ samāgamya tayā sahāste
english: The king said 'Very well', united with her, and dwelt together with her.

sanskrit: tatraivāsīne rājani senānvagacchat padenānupadaṃ dṛṣṭvā rājānaṃ parivāryātiṣṭhat
english: As the king sat there, his army followed step by step; seeing the king, they surrounded him and stood guard.

sanskrit: paryāśvastaś ca rājā tayaiva saha śibikayā prāyād avighāṭitayā svanagaram anuprāpya rahasi tayā saha ramann āste nānyat kiṃ canāpaśyat
english: The king, comforted, went with her in a covered litter, and reaching his own city he lived privately sporting with her alone, seeing nothing else.

sanskrit: atha pradhānāmātyas tasyābhyāśacarāḥ striyo 'pṛcchat kim atra prayojanaṃ vartata iti
english: Then the chief minister asked the women who attended close to him: 'What purpose is being served here?'

sanskrit: athābruvaṃs tāḥ striyaḥ apūrvam iva paśyāma udakaṃ nātra nīyateti
english: Those women said: 'We observe something unprecedented — no water is brought here.'

sanskrit: athāmātyo 'nudakaṃ vanaṃ kārayitvodāravṛkṣaṃ bahumūlapuṣpaphalaṃ rahasy upagamya rājānam abravīt vanam idam udāram anudakam sādhv atra ramyatām iti
english: Then the minister had a grove made without water, with noble trees bearing many roots, flowers, and fruits, and approaching the king in private said: 'This grove is magnificent and waterless — it is well to take pleasure here.'

sanskrit: sa tasya vacanāt tayaiva saha devyā tad vanaṃ prāviśat sa kadā cit tasmin vane ramye tayaiva saha vyavaharat atha kṣuttṛṣṇārditaḥ śrānto 'timātram atimuktāgāram apaśyat
english: At his words, he entered that grove together with the queen. One day, sporting with her in that beautiful grove, he became excessively worn out by hunger and thirst and saw a jasmine bower.

sanskrit: tat praviśya rājā saha priyayā sudhātalasukṛtāṃ vimalasalilapūrṇāṃ vāpīm apaśyat
english: Entering it with his beloved, the king saw a well built with a smooth plaster floor, filled with clear water.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvaiva ca tāṃ tasyā eva tīre sahaiva tayā devyā vyatiṣṭhat
english: And seeing it, he stood with the queen on its very bank.

sanskrit: atha tāṃ devīṃ sa rājābravīt sādhv avatara vāpīsalilam iti
english: Then the king said to the queen: 'Please, descend into the water of the well.'

sanskrit: sā tadvacaḥ śrutvāvatīrya vāpīṃ nyamajjat na punar udamajjat
english: Hearing his words, she descended and plunged into the well and did not rise again.

sanskrit: tāṃ mṛgayamāṇo rājā nāpaśyat
english: The king searched for her but did not find her.

sanskrit: vāpīm api niḥsrāvya maṇḍūkaṃ śvabhramukhe dṛṣṭvā kruddha ājñāpayām āsa sarvamaṇḍūkavadhaḥ kriyatām iti yo mayārthī sa mṛtakair maṇḍūkair upāyanair mām upatiṣṭhed iti
english: He even had the well drained, and seeing a frog at the mouth of a rat-hole, furious he commanded: 'Let a slaughter of all frogs be carried out; whoever seeks favour from me should approach me with the gift of dead frogs.'

sanskrit: atha maṇḍūkavadhe ghore kriyamāṇe dikṣu sarvāsu maṇḍūkān bhayam āviśat te bhītā maṇḍūkarājñe yathāvṛttaṃ nyavedayan
english: Then, as the terrible slaughter of frogs was being carried out in all directions, fear seized all the frogs; terrified, they reported the whole event to the king of frogs.

sanskrit: tato maṇḍūkarāṭ tāpasaveṣadhārī rājānam abhyagacchat
english: Then the king of frogs, wearing the garb of an ascetic, approached the king.
